title: Make the Match Decision
subtitle: Route the invoice on the results, not on a hunch
scenario: It is 11:30 AM. Two records decide this invoice's path: the three-way match (matched, within tolerance, quantity exact) and the duplicate check (not a duplicate). This is the fork in the workflow. Encode the rule that sends a clean invoice to auto-approval - and would send anything else to the exception queue.
input: Three-Way Match: withinTolerance true, qtyMatch true, matchResult matched. Duplicate Check: isDuplicate false. Rule: if the line is within tolerance AND quantities match AND it is not a duplicate, route to auto-approve; otherwise route to the exception queue for a human.
instructions: Restate the three inputs the decision reads: withinTolerance, qtyMatch, isDuplicate.
Apply the rule: all three clean means auto-approve; any failure means exception.
Set route to the path this clean invoice takes.
Return one valid JSON object. Use true/false for the flags.
copilotPrompt: Produce a match-decision JSON record: withinTolerance, qtyMatch, isDuplicate, and route. Route to auto-approve only when within tolerance, quantities match, and it is not a duplicate; otherwise route to the exception queue.
successMessage: Decision made. Clean on all three checks, INV-58831 routes to auto-approval.
editorHelper: Apply the fork rule to the two upstream results.

sections.title: One decision, two paths
sections.body: Every invoice reaches this fork. Clean lines flow to auto-approval; anything unusual goes to the exception queue for a human. The decision is the map's only branch.

sections.title: Route on results, not vibes
sections.body: The decision reads three booleans from upstream - withinTolerance, qtyMatch, isDuplicate. Because the inputs are already computed, the routing is a rule, not a judgment call.

sections.title: All clean means auto-approve
sections.body: INV-58831 is within tolerance, quantities match, and it is not a duplicate. All three green means it earns the auto-approve path - no human needed today.

sections.title: Any failure means exception
sections.body: Flip any one of the three and the same rule routes to the exception queue instead. Encoding the fork once is what makes both outcomes consistent and auditable.

takeaway.heading: Match decision made
points: You encoded the workflow's one fork as a rule over three upstream booleans.
Within tolerance, quantities matched, and not a duplicate - all three green - so INV-58831 routes to auto-approve.
Flipping any single input would route the same rule to the exception queue instead.
Routing on computed results, not judgment, is what makes both outcomes consistent and auditable.
The workflow can now send clean invoices to auto-approval and exceptions to a human, automatically.
